items.claim: The unit's own front-seam argument is contradicted by the bytes it quotes, and its one disclosed cross-seam cohesion device misdescribes the verse it appeals to.
items.evidence: The rationale calls the incoming population 'unconnected to the captains already at Mizpah', then splices a verse whose first word is the additive particle וְגַ֣ם (oshb:Jer.40.11, byte) - a verse-initial 'and also' that explicitly attaches this group to the party immediately preceding, i.e. a byte-true continuity signal straddling the unit's own front seam which the row does not disclose as cohesion while it does disclose a different one. Second, the disclosed device is stated as 'the same pairing Gedaliah had just instructed the field captains to gather at oshb:Jer.40.10', but oshb:Jer.40.10 carries a three-item list, יַ֨יִן וְקַ֜יִץ וְשֶׁ֗מֶן (byte) - wine, summer fruit and oil, matching the second witness at “gather wine and summer fruits and oil” (web:Jer.40.10) - against the two-item יַ֥יִן וָקַ֖יִץ (oshb:Jer.40.12, byte); the two are not even byte-identical in the word they share, the conjunction carrying sheva at oshb:Jer.40.10 and qamats at oshb:Jer.40.12. The 40:10 form is not spliced anywhere in the row and the recurrence carries no tier label, so a recurrence claim is asserted with no quoted form behind it. Declared heuristic false positives on this row (the bracketing-word hits) are confirmed as such; these are separate defects. The span itself is not contested.

items.claim: The ketiv/qere disclosure names a letter that is not in the bytes, misdescribing a note the row itself offers as a boundary corroborator at the unit's closing verse.
items.evidence: The bytes at oshb:Jer.40.16 read תעש תַּעֲשֵׂ֖ה (byte). The ketiv is three letters, tav-ayin-shin, which the row states correctly; the qere is four letters, tav-ayin-shin(with sin dot)-he. The row instead describes it as a tav-ayin-shin-he-yod qere, adding a fifth letter, yod, that no codepoint in the verse supports. This sits inside the book ketiv/qere inventory of 141 notes over 124 verses and the note is presented alongside the closing mark as joint warrant for the unit's end, so the letter-level error lands on load-bearing prose. Everything else in the row verifies: all four splices reach byte tier at their cited refs, the closing mark is correctly typed as setumah, and the exclusivity claim for Baalis is genuinely backed - the consonantal sweep returns that name in exactly 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse), so the row's own digit is right and its declared heuristic false positives are confirmed. The span itself is not contested.

items.claim: The unit verifies on the bytes: 3 splices at byte tier, 2 seg-layer marks in the span plus the front-seam mark disclosed under their correct types, and the date-object distinction drawn honestly.
items.evidence: The opening splice carries בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י (oshb:Jer.41.1, byte), a month notice, and the row is right to hold it apart from the book's classified reign-year date object rather than folding it in - that object is built on the year-word and bet-plus-cardinal shapes, and this site is not a member of it. Both paseq notes in the span (oshb:Jer.41.1, oshb:Jer.41.2) are disclosed count-only with no position claim, the front-seam mark at oshb:Jer.40.16 is disclosed under the correct setumah type, and oshb:Jer.41.3 carries no mark, so the span-relevant disclosure is complete. The pedigree claim is byte-true: מִזֶּ֣רַע הַ֠מְּלוּכָה וְרַבֵּ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.41.1, byte), and the royal-offspring noun occurs in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse), so the detail genuinely does not recur where the name does. Declared heuristic false positives on this row are confirmed - all four declared hits fall inside quoted witness text or ordinary narrative wording. One non-driving observation: the closing device sentence locates the non-repetition by pointing at neighbouring units positionally rather than by verse anchor, which is looser than the verse-anchored convention; it changes no byte finding and does not affect this verdict.

items.claim: The unit reads the same single-witness seg layer two ways inside one span - corroboration where it agrees, bare texture where it would cut - and leaves one full-verse splice with no second-witness rendering at all.
items.evidence: Two marks of identical type fall in this span: one closing oshb:Jer.41.6 and one closing oshb:Jer.41.10. The row cites the second as corroboration for its own end boundary while disclosing the first only as texture, without naming the internal seam after oshb:Jer.41.6 that the same layer would equally support; under the weak-tier posture neither can drive a boundary, so citing one for the reading adopted and not engaging the other's contrary implication is asymmetric use of one layer inside one span. Second, oshb:Jer.41.9 is spliced in full - וְהַבּ֗וֹר אֲשֶׁר֩ הִשְׁלִ֨יךְ ... (byte) - with no paired second-witness rendering anywhere in the row; of this cluster 28 full-verse splices, 27 carry a second-witness rendering and this 1 does not. It is not forced by the nesting constraint that shortens the other glosses here, because that verse carries no internal quotation in the second witness. Third, the seam driver at oshb:Jer.41.4 is called a date notice with none of the object-distinction given to the month notice at oshb:Jer.41.1: its bytes read בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשֵּׁנִ֖י לְהָמִ֣ית אֶת גְּדַלְיָ֑הוּ (byte), a relative-day back-reference that names the preceding unit's own event rather than any member of the book's classified date object. All eight splices reach byte tier, the Shiloh form is handled correctly against the attested spelling with no cross-site count offered, and the declared heuristic false positives are confirmed. The span itself is not contested; the held question at verse 10 is honest and the confidence posture fits it.

items.claim: The closing device claim is byte-false: it makes Gibeon the place the abduction was heading away from, but Gibeon is not named anywhere in the abduction report.
items.evidence: The row states that the interception site is 'the same site Ishmael's abduction had been heading away from'. The bytes do not support it. The abduction report locates the seizure at Mizpah, אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמִּצְפָּ֗ה (oshb:Jer.41.10, byte), and states its destination as וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ לַעֲבֹ֖ר אֶל בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן (oshb:Jer.41.10, byte) - toward the children of Ammon. The place-name first enters the narrative at the interception itself, אֶל מַ֥יִם רַבִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּגִבְעֽוֹן (oshb:Jer.41.12, byte), and its only other appearance in this arc is the retrospective notice at oshb:Jer.41.16; the consonantal sweep returns the name in 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses), the third an origin phrase at oshb:Jer.28.1 far outside this narrative. So the site named as the point of departure is not the point of departure in the bytes. A second, softer overstatement rides in the same sentence: the closing mark is said to close Ishmael's part in the account, yet the name still stands in oshb:Jer.41.16 and oshb:Jer.41.18 (byte), retrospectively but present. The five splices all reach byte tier, the closing mark and the front-seam mark are correctly typed and no mark in the span is left undisclosed, and the declared heuristic false positives are confirmed. The span itself is not contested.

items.claim: An exclusivity claim is dampened with a witness label instead of the sweep digit it requires, and the closing seam argument asserts a first occurrence the bytes contradict three times over.
items.evidence: The device sentence says the place is 'named only here in the book' and offers '(single-witness)' where a digit-bearing sweep is owed; a witness or tier label proves the quote, not the exclusivity. The underlying fact does hold - בְּגֵר֣וּת כמוהם כִּמְהָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.41.17, byte), and the consonantal sweeps return the place noun in 1 verse, the qere name in 1 verse and the ketiv form in 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse each) - so this is a disclosure defect, not a false fact, while the same digit convention is met for the single-site name at oshb:Jer.40.14, so the declared heuristic-false-positive disposition on this hit is refuted rather than confirmed. Separately, the closing sentence claims the field captains become the account's subject together for the first time at oshb:Jer.42.1. The bytes contradict it: the phrase stands in 9 verses book-wide (sweep: 9 verses), and the captains are joint subject with Johanan of the finite verb already at וְיֽוֹחָנָן֙ בֶּן קָרֵ֔חַ וְכָל שָׂרֵ֥י הַחֲיָלִ֖ים ... (oshb:Jer.40.13, byte), at וַיִּשְׁמַע֙ יוֹחָנָ֣ן בֶּן קָרֵ֔חַ וְכָל שָׂרֵ֥י הַחֲיָלִ֖ים (oshb:Jer.41.11, byte), and at וַיִּקַּח֩ יוֹחָנָ֨ן בֶּן קָרֵ֜חַ וְכָל שָׂרֵ֧י הַחֲיָלִ֣ים (oshb:Jer.41.16, byte) - this row's own opening verse. What is genuinely new at oshb:Jer.42.1 is only the word order, וַֽיִּגְּשׁוּ֙ כָּל שָׂרֵ֣י הַחֲיָלִ֔ים (byte), fronting the captains ahead of Johanan; that is a defensible seam observation and is not what the row claims. The three splices reach byte tier, the ketiv/qere pair is quoted exactly as the bytes carry it, and the note and mark inside the span and the front-seam mark are all disclosed. The span itself is not contested.

items.claim: The two-name-form claim states that both spellings are given as the bytes carry them, yet the row splices 1 of the 2 forms, and the two figures are separated on the strength of an English rendering rather than the Hebrew.
items.evidence: The row asserts of two similarly named figures that 'both spellings are given as the bytes actually carry them'. The row splices 1 of those 2 forms - וִֽיזַנְיָ֖ה בֶּן הוֹשַֽׁעְיָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.42.1, byte), inside the opening splice. The second form is absent from all 22 fields of the row, and it is not the same spelling: oshb:Jer.40.8 carries וִֽיזַנְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן הַמַּ֣עֲכָתִ֔י (byte), the long form closing he-vav, against the short form closing he at oshb:Jer.42.1. The difference is exactly the long-versus-short name-form class this book keeps live, and it is invisible in the second witness, which renders both as the same English word - “Jezaniah the son of the Maacathite” (web:Jer.40.8) beside “Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah” (web:Jer.42.1) - so as written the distinction rests on the patronymics in translation while the actual byte-level spelling difference goes unstated in a field that claims to have stated it. The reference itself is properly carried in the evidence list, and the rest of the row verifies: three byte-tier splices, the front-seam mark correctly typed, and the negative mark statement accurate - the inventory carries no mark at oshb:Jer.42.1, oshb:Jer.42.2 or oshb:Jer.42.3. Declared heuristic false positives are confirmed as such; this is a separate defect inside one of those sentences. The span itself is not contested.

items.claim: The unit's internal-cohesion argument rests on a syntactic form claim that neither witness supports.
items.evidence: The row calls the reply 'one unbroken sentence'. The splice it labels byte tier begins with the narrative frame וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם יִרְמְיָ֤הוּ הַנָּבִיא֙ (oshb:Jer.42.4, byte) - a wayyiqtol frame plus subject standing outside the speech it introduces - and the verse divides internally at כְּדִבְרֵיכֶ֑ם (byte), which carries the etnachta; the second witness renders the same verse with three internal full stops, opening “I have heard you.” (web:Jer.42.4). No morphology or syntax layer is staged, so a sentence-level form label cannot be machine-checked and has to stand on the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings; here both cut against it, so the claim should be held rather than asserted. The operative half of the same sentence is byte-true and the boundary is sound: the speaker changes on both sides, the preceding verse closing the petition and the following verse opening a fresh reported-speech frame, וְהֵ֨מָּה֙ אָמְר֣וּ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.42.5, byte). The negative disclosure is accurate - no mark, note or seg entry stands at oshb:Jer.42.3, oshb:Jer.42.4 or oshb:Jer.42.5, the next being at oshb:Jer.42.6 - and the single-verse span is written in the full X-X form. Declared heuristic false positives are confirmed. The span itself is not contested.
